description: The standing window set of the pre-release noop (AGENTS.md, Validation), for both balance packages, evm-balances-native and evm-balances-erc20: the windows are blocks of each chain, not of a package. Each window is a range of complete 1000-block segments: start inclusive, stop exclusive, run as `substreams run <spkg> db_out -e <chain>.substreams.pinax.network:443 --noop-mode --production-mode --limit-processed-blocks 0 -s <start> -t <stop>`. Chains are Pinax endpoint names: eth, bsc, base, arbone, optimism, polygon, unichain, hyperevm.
origin: Tightened on 2026-11-04 for ERC-20 v0.7.5 from the 100,000-block windows of the native v0.7.11 pre-release matrix (docs/history/native-v0711-prerelease-2026-10-29.json), whose per-window reasons were not recorded. Its event windows start 10,000 blocks before their event's segment (Ethereum's forks and refusals and BSC's forks show it), so each 100,000-block window keeps its first segment and the two segments at start + 9,000 and start + 10,000; its 1000-block segments are kept whole, and its continuous catch-up runs keep their last segment. 48.8 million blocks became about 1.2 million.

selection.event: the segment before and at a hard fork, network upgrade or past refusal
selection.sample: a sample of an era of each chain, or its first segment (genesis; Optimism 105,236,000; Arbitrum One 22,208,000)
selection.segment: a 1000-block segment named by an investigation
selection.head: the last segment below a head at an earlier release, where a live sink started or could start
selection.block: the segment of a block a release's investigation replayed

at_each_release: Run every window of this file.
Add each chain's last complete 1000-block segment below its current head, and below the live sink's planned start where that differs.
Add the segments of every block the release changes rows for or newly refuses, and of each new hard fork or upgrade: the segment before its activation and the segment of its activation.

A native release that can refuse blocks the previous one accepts (a new persistence or continuity check) also runs the whole range where that shape can occur, continuously, as native v0.7.11 and v0.7.12 did for Polygon's Block.ver 3 range after Napoli; a sample of segments cannot show that no block refuses.
Append the added windows here in the release's record pull request, and record the run under docs/history/.
